label: Fires at GO after a2-rare-S1-rewarded trials, only around episode trials 70-89.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S1 r') * (ep_trial >= 70) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S1 r') * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S1 r') * (tv('reward', -2) == 1)
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (ep_trial >= 70) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (ep_trial >= 60) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (ep_trial >= 80) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (ep_trial >= 60) * (tv("state", -2) == 1)
explanation: Silent at D1 and D2. At GO, magnitude is driven almost entirely by the previous trial being a2 -> S1 (rare) rewarded, gated by episode time: near zero before ~trial 60, large (~0.4-0.9) in trials ~70-89, weaker again at trials 90+. Within those trials it is larger when the ideal-observer belief leans toward S2 (negative weight on belief_lo, i.e. the rare reward is more surprising / evidence for S1). Other previous-trial patterns slightly lower it. The free fit adds a finer episode-time ramp (60/80 steps), a small boost if the trial before was also rewarded, and a slight decrease if the trial before reached S1. Residual misses: some GO firing on window-first trials (previous trial unknown) and occasional firing after a1 S1 r late in the episode. Uses no future, hidden or model-output variables.

issues: The label says 'only around episode trials 70-89', but the short form does not say that. The fitted weights are +0.568 for ep>=70 and -0.345 for ep>=90, so from trial 90 on the predicted firing after a2 S1 r is still about 40% of the 70-89 level. The worst misses are in fact GO steps after a2 S1 r at t90-93 where the actual value is 0.66-0.98 and the prediction is about 0.17-0.27. Firing at 90+ is under-predicted, not absent.
The label leaves out the third short-form term (belief_lo, weight -0.027), so the label and short form do not match. That term is also weak: dropping it lowers test R^2 only from 0.518 to 0.501.

The belief_lo term is not the best third factor. Replacing it with 'trial before also rewarded', (tv('reward',-2)==1), gives test 0.529 against 0.518. belief<0.5 gives 0.517, state(-2)==S2 gives 0.508 and belief_cover gives 0.504. So 'more surprising rare reward' is a weaker story than 'two rewarded trials in a row'.

Core claims check out. Activation is exactly zero at D1 and D2. In the residual table, a2 S1 r at GO is +0.16 and every other previous-trial pattern is about -0.005 to -0.012. Gating by ep>=70 (rather than a linear ep_trial term: 0.379) is what lifts the score above the additive ceiling of 0.21. Adding an ep>=60 step only adds 0.003.

Remaining systematic misses are mostly firing on the window's first trial (the previous trial is unknown; a prev_action==-1 x late term adds nothing beyond the timing baseline) and smaller firing (0.2-0.4) after a1 S1 r late in the episode (adding a1 S1 r x ep>=70 adds nothing on test, 0.502). The misses summary puts the largest per-cell error at +0.021 for GO after a2 S1 r, i.e. under-prediction concentrated in the target cell. No large uncaptured error class outside it.
